$schema.description: Editor hint only; ignored by the loader.

notes.description: Why these values (feel targets, references), for owner review.

selectRange.description: Farthest a target can be picked or cycled to, m (eye to lock point).

coneAngle.description: Pick and cycle only targets within this angle of the camera forward, degrees.

breakRange.description: The lock breaks once the target is farther than this, m; ≥ selectRange.

lostSightMs.description: The lock breaks once the target has been out of sight this long, ms; sight returning sooner keeps it.

switchRange.description: When the locked target dies, the lock moves to the best other target this close, m, or releases.

eyeHeight.description: Height above the player’s feet that sight lines and angles are measured from, m.

minVisibility.description: A lock point is in sight when at least this much of its sight line is clear, 0–1.

distanceWeight.description: Picking scores angle ÷ coneAngle + distanceWeight × distance ÷ selectRange (lowest wins); 0 ignores distance.

priorityWeight.description: Each point of a target’s priority takes this much off its pick score.

turnRate.description: How fast the locked player turns to face the target, degrees/s.

stickThreshold.description: Right-stick sideways deflection that counts as a flick, 0.1–1.

stickRest.description: The stick must come back within this sideways deflection before the next flick, 0–0.9; below stickThreshold.

mouseCounts.description: Sideways mouse movement in one tick that counts as a flick, counts.

mouseRest.description: Sideways mouse movement in one tick at or below which the mouse is at rest, counts; below mouseCounts.

flick.description: Cycling by flicking look input sideways while locked on: the right stick (the pad has no cycle button) or a fast mouse swipe.

time.description: Seconds for the camera to swing about two thirds of the way to its lock-on framing (exponential ease), and back on release.

targetWeight.description: Where between the player’s head (0) and the target’s lock point (1) the camera aims.

pitchOffset.description: Added to the aim pitch, degrees; negative looks further down so the player stays in frame.

framing.description: Camera framing while locked (presentation only): keeps the player and target in view.
